newsitem.title: GERMANY: German prisoner takes worker hostage, police say.
newsitem.headline: German prisoner takes worker hostage, police say.

text.p: A 37-year-old German prisoner was holding a 43-year-old prison worker hostage in the hospital of a jail in the eastern town of Naumburg, authorities said on Sunday.

The prison worker was taken hostage on Saturday afternoon by the man, who is serving a sentence for attempted murder and not eligible for parole until 2002. The prisoner pulled out a sharp object and forced the worker into the prison hospital with him.
Police said they had not had any contact with the hostage-taker. Naumburg is about 160 km (100 miles) south of Berlin.

A spokesman said the hostage-taker had not answered the telephone nor responded to other attempts by authorities to establish communications. He said they did not know what the hostage-taker was demanding.

Police said they wanted to negotiate with the hostage-taker rather than storm the building. They said he most likely would have obtained access to drugs and medical equipment in the hospital that could endanger the prison worker.
The prison in Naumburg holds 300 prisoners and is the largest in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.
